items.headline: E-Infrastructure Solutions revenue rose 192% in Q2 2026
items.summary: E-Infrastructure Solutions revenue was $905.0 million in Q2 2026 versus $310.4 million in Q2 2025, driven by large mission-critical projects and the CEC acquisition, which contributed $239.9 million of revenue in the quarter.
items.implication: Continued demand from data center and mission-critical customers could support further revenue growth if large projects continue to be awarded and executed on schedule.
items.detail: Six-month E-Infrastructure revenue was $1.50 billion versus $528.7 million a year earlier, an increase of 184%. Segment operating income was $210.8 million (23.3% of revenue) in Q2 2026 versus $83.8 million (27.0%) in Q2 2025.
items.impact_basis: This segment is now 78% of consolidated Q2 2026 revenue and drove nearly all of the company-wide revenue increase, making it the dominant determinant of near-term results.
items.quote: Revenues were $905.0 million for the second quarter of 2026, an increase of $594.6 million, or 192%, compared to the second quarter of 2025.

items.headline: Total backlog reached $4.33 billion at June 30, 2026
items.summary: Total Backlog (RPOs plus MSAs) was $4.33 billion at June 30, 2026, up from $3.01 billion at December 31, 2025; Combined Backlog including Unsigned Awards was $5.62 billion, with a six-month book-to-burn ratio of 2.3X.
items.implication: A growing backlog and book-to-burn ratio above 1.0 may indicate continued revenue growth over the 6-to-36-month typical contract completion period, though realization is not guaranteed.
items.detail: RPOs were $4.23 billion and MSAs were $100.0 million at June 30, 2026, versus RPOs of $3.01 billion and no MSAs at December 31, 2025. Unsigned Awards were $1.28 billion at June 30, 2026 versus $300.7 million at year-end 2025.
items.impact_basis: Backlog growth is substantial relative to trailing revenue, but conversion timing and realization are uncertain and backlog is not a GAAP-recognized or guaranteed revenue measure.
items.quote: At June 30, 2026, our RPOs were $4.23 billion and our MSAs were $100.0 million, resulting in a total Backlog of $4.33 billion.

items.headline: Credit facility expanded to $1.5 billion, extended to 2031
items.summary: On July 2, 2026, Sterling entered a Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement increasing revolving borrowing capacity by $1.05 billion to $1.5 billion and extending maturity to July 2, 2031; $90 million was outstanding as of that date.
items.implication: Expanded, longer-dated credit capacity could support further acquisitions, capital expenditures, and share repurchases without near-term refinancing pressure.
items.detail: The agreement includes an incremental facility option of up to the greater of $500 million or 100% of EBITDA, plus additional capacity subject to a leverage test, and eliminates the prior SOFR 10bp credit spread adjustment.
items.impact_basis: The facility materially increases available liquidity relative to the $292.5 million outstanding under the prior agreement at December 31, 2025, but usage and effect on results depend on future draws and acquisitions.
items.quote: The Amended Credit Agreement increases borrowing capacity by $1.05 billion and will initially provide for revolving borrowings up to an aggregate principal amount of $1.5 billion

items.headline: Two acquisitions expanded E-Infrastructure Solutions in 2025-2026
items.summary: Sterling acquired CEC Facilities Group for $561.6 million (September 2025) and Stone Ridge Contracting for $178.0 million (June 2026), both placed in the E-Infrastructure Solutions segment, with combined earn-outs of up to $95 million.
items.implication: Successful integration could add scale and electrical/mechanical and site-development capabilities, but acquisition costs and earn-out obligations add near-term expense and integration risk.
items.detail: CEC was funded with $442.9 million cash and $79.5 million stock, with up to $80 million earn-out tied to operating income targets. Stone Ridge was funded with $140.0 million cash and $27.4 million stock, with up to $15 million earn-out tied to EBITDA.
items.impact_basis: Combined purchase price of roughly $740 million is sizable relative to the company's balance sheet and already contributed $37.5 million of operating income in the first half of 2026, but integration success is not yet proven.
items.quote: On June 1, 2026, Sterling acquired substantially all of the assets of Pocatello, Idaho-based Stone Ridge Contracting, LLC... The purchase price was $178.0 million

items.headline: Board authorized up to $400 million stock repurchase program
items.summary: Effective November 12, 2025, the Board approved a program to repurchase up to $400 million of common stock over 24 months, to be funded with cash on hand and operating cash flow; $35.3 million was repurchased in the six months ended June 30, 2026.
items.implication: Continued repurchases could reduce share count and return capital to shareholders, though timing and completion are discretionary and not guaranteed.
items.detail: The program replaced a prior $200 million program approved December 5, 2023. Repurchases will diminish cash reserves and the program may be suspended or discontinued at the company's discretion.
items.impact_basis: Program authorization is sizable but repurchases to date ($35.3 million in H1 2026) are small relative to operating cash flow of $328.0 million for the same period.
items.quote: Effective November 12, 2025, the Board of Directors approved a program authorizing us to repurchase up to $400 million of our outstanding common stock over a 24-month period

items.headline: Backlog realization not guaranteed, grew to $3.01 billion
items.summary: Backlog at December 31, 2025 totaled $3.01 billion, up from $1.69 billion at December 31, 2024; the company states it has no contractual right to backlog revenue if projects are cancelled, terminated, or scope-adjusted.
items.implication: Reported backlog growth may overstate future revenue certainty if customers cancel, delay, or adjust project scope.
items.detail: The filing notes backlog should not be viewed as a stand-alone indicator and that timing of contract awards, duration of large contracts, and service mix can significantly affect backlog reporting.
items.impact_basis: Backlog nearly doubled year over year and is a key forward indicator for the company, but the company explicitly disclaims assurance that it will convert to revenue or earnings.
items.quote: Backlog as of December 31, 2025 totaled $3.01 billion.

items.headline: Goodwill and intangibles rose sharply to $1.14 billion combined
items.summary: Goodwill was approximately $585 million and intangibles approximately $555 million at December 31, 2025, up from $265 million and $316 million, respectively, at December 31, 2024, raising impairment exposure.
items.implication: A decline in market capitalization or acquired business performance could require a goodwill or intangible asset write-down, reducing reported net earnings and equity.
items.detail: The increase reflects recent acquisitions including CEC. The filing states write-downs, if required, may be substantial and could materially adversely affect net earnings and equity.
items.impact_basis: Combined goodwill and intangibles of $1.14 billion represent a large share of total assets following recent acquisitions, though no impairment has been recorded as of the filing date.
items.quote: We had approximately $585 million of goodwill and $555 million of intangibles recorded on our Consolidated Balance Sheet at December 31, 2025.

items.headline: Credit agreement restricts additional debt, pledges nearly all assets
items.summary: Sterling pledged substantially all assets as collateral under its amended and restated Credit Agreement (originally dated June 5, 2025) with $292.5 million outstanding at December 31, 2025, and must obtain lender consent for most additional debt.
items.implication: Collateral pledges and covenant restrictions could limit financing flexibility for future acquisitions or capital needs if liquidity requirements increase.
items.detail: The Credit Agreement was set to mature June 5, 2028, as of the 10-K; it was later amended and extended per a subsequent 8-K. Covenants restrict liens, additional indebtedness, dividends, and asset sales.
items.impact_basis: The company states it believes it has resources to meet obligations, and the facility was later expanded and extended, reducing near-term liquidity concern.
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, our aggregate principal amount outstanding under the Credit Agreement was $292.5 million.

items.headline: Joint venture exposure to unconsolidated contracts nearly tripled
items.summary: At December 31, 2025, approximately $371.9 million of construction work remained on unconsolidated joint venture contracts, with Sterling's proportionate share at $148.8 million, versus $150.3 million and $73.6 million, respectively, at December 31, 2024.
items.implication: If a joint venture partner fails to perform, Sterling could be fully liable for the partner's share of remaining work under joint and several liability provisions.
items.detail: The company states it is not currently aware of any situation requiring it to fulfill a partner's responsibilities, but the exposure has grown materially year over year.
items.impact_basis: Proportionate share of $148.8 million is a moderate figure relative to total assets, and the company reports no current instance of partner default.
items.quote: At December 31, 2025, there was approximately $371.9 million of construction work to be completed on unconsolidated construction joint venture contracts, of which $148.8 million represented our proportionate share.

items.headline: New risk factors added covering AI, data privacy, and permitting
items.summary: The 10-K added new risk factors on data privacy/cybersecurity law compliance, use of artificial intelligence technologies with unproven commercialization, and the need to obtain and maintain numerous government permits and licenses.
items.implication: Evolving legal and regulatory requirements in these areas could increase compliance costs or disrupt operations if permits are denied or AI investments fail to generate returns.
items.detail: The AI risk factor notes the company uses third-party AI tools and is developing its own AI strategy but faces an evolving market and unproven growth prospects; permitting risk factors are newly detailed as standalone items.
items.impact_basis: These are newly articulated risks without disclosed financial impact to date, and the filing frames them as general, forward-looking compliance exposures.
items.quote: We use artificial intelligence ("AI") technologies in our business, and the deployment, use, and maintenance of these technologies involve significant technological and legal risks.

items.headline: Building Solutions operating income fell on residential downturn
items.summary: Building Solutions operating income was $14.7 million (7.3% of revenue) for the six months ended June 30, 2026, down $7.5 million from $22.2 million (11.1% of revenue) in the same period of 2025, due to continued residential market weakness.
items.implication: Continued affordability pressure on homebuyers may keep this segment's margins below prior-year levels for an extended period.
items.detail: Revenue in the segment was roughly flat (up $2.3 million for the six months) while operating income declined, indicating margin compression rather than a revenue problem specifically.
items.impact_basis: The segment is about 10% of consolidated H1 2026 revenue, so the decline has a contained effect on overall company results even though the percentage decline is meaningful.
items.quote: Operating income was $14.7 million, or 7.3% of revenue, for the six months ended June 30, 2026, a decrease of $7.5 million, compared to $22.2 million, or 11.1% of revenue, for the six months ended June 30, 2025.

items.headline: Transportation Solutions revenue declined on lower heavy highway work
items.summary: Transportation Solutions revenue was $289.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, down $27.9 million, or 9%, from the same period in 2025, driven by lower heavy highway and other revenue.
items.implication: A continued shift away from low-bid heavy highway work could pressure segment revenue even as operating margin improves on project mix.
items.detail: Despite the revenue decline, operating income increased to $42.9 million (14.8% of revenue) from $37.2 million (11.7% of revenue), reflecting improved project margin mix.
items.impact_basis: Revenue decline is modest in dollar terms and offset by margin improvement, and the company describes this as a deliberate strategic shift rather than a demand problem.
items.quote: Revenues were $289.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, a decrease of $27.9 million, or 9%, compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025.

items.headline: Investing cash outflows nearly tripled on acquisitions and capex
items.summary: Net cash used in investing activities was $206.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, versus $66.5 million a year earlier, driven by $140.0 million for acquisitions (Stone Ridge) and $69.6 million for capital equipment purchases.
items.implication: Higher acquisition and capex spending reduces cash on hand, which could affect flexibility for further acquisitions or repurchases if operating cash flow growth slows.
items.detail: The outflow was partly offset by $3.1 million of proceeds from asset sales; generally available cash was $306.9 million at June 30, 2026, down slightly from $314.6 million at December 31, 2025.
items.impact_basis: Operating cash flow of $328.0 million for the same six-month period comfortably covered investing outflows, limiting near-term liquidity concern.
items.quote: During the six months ended June 30, 2026, net cash used in investing activities was $206.5 million, compared to net cash used of $66.5 million in the six months ended June 30, 2025.
